limits: Pre-RINIT session consumer ordering requires native instrumentation/source review; session-key absence alone is insufficient.
Startup OOM precedes user script registration; user shutdown/destructor absence there is not proof of _exit.
HTTP globals/handler checks cover observable request state, not all internal lifecycle fields.
Linux NTS FPM; tested callbacks and session consumers only. Third-party callbacks not loaded.
Observer uses stack formatting and OS append writes; instrumentation may change timing. Original uninstrumented gates remain separate.
This run closes the pre-RINIT session consumer evidence gap for these requests, not all CVE/OOM lifecycle coverage.
Sequence is event order, not elapsed time.
PASS means required observed checks met their own expectations; legacy PASS is not a security verdict.
No report establishes all CVE variants as fixed.
